conventions.interval: point estimate [2.5th, 97.5th bootstrap percentile], B = 2000 unless stated
conventions.point: metric on the full population; mean over repetitions/seeds for CV settings and the GRU
conventions.AgentDrift_bootstrap: stratified trajectory-level (plan 3.5); world clusters as sensitivity
conventions.paired: all methods of one table share the resampled rows and the drawn repetition/seed
conventions.pool_E: AgentDrift benign + hard_negative + attacked; AgentDojo P0 (benign + compromised)
conventions.wAUPRC@pi: prevalence-weighted average precision (plan 3.1), positives weighted pi/(1-pi) n_neg/n_pos
conventions.thresholds: t_r80 from training data only (20th percentile of training-positive scores)
conventions.filler_sentence: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.

M5_1_coefficients.note: all detectors standardize features with StandardScaler before the logistic regression, so the fitted coefficients are standardized coefficients (log-odds change per training-set SD).
M5_1_coefficients.R1_bootstrap_note: 500 refits on stratified resamples of data/train.jsonl, benign tool vocabulary of the original training set; point = cached fit; 74 s
M5_1_coefficients.P0all_note: within-AgentDojo model fitted on all 2,686 P0 rows (same recipe; vocabulary from the 392 benign traces); 500 cluster-bootstrap refits over 117 suite|user_task clusters. This is a descriptive fit, not one of the WUT fold models.

M5_1_univariate.reversal_definition: detected reversal: the 95% interval lies above 0.5 in one population and below 0.5 in the other (AgentDojo intervals: cluster bootstrap)

within_minus_transfer.holm_family: within minus transfer, over the 5 detectors of this table (plan family d restricted)

eval.population: R1 pool E (padded attacked, unpadded negatives)
R1 pool E (padded attacked, unpadded negatives); 3 seeds

primary.population: WUT P0 (padded compromised traces, unpadded benign), suite|user_task clusters

located_subset.population: WUT P0 restricted to benign + compromised traces with a located injected step

location.method: raw run file runs/<model>/<suite>/<user_task>/<attack_type>/<injection_task>.json; a step is an injected step if its observation contains the first or last 60 alphanumeric characters (lower case, escapes removed) of any value of `injections`

M5_4_truncation.agentdojo_share_beyond_agentdrift_note: AgentDrift maximum over the pooled 10,656 train+test trajectories; intervals: cluster bootstrap over suite|user_task, B = 2000; failed-attack shares are descriptive (no interval)

corrected_failed.note: v0.3 did not extract unsuccessful attacks

keyword_vs_annotation_agentdrift.ci_note: tool-level counts are a census of the vocabulary (no sampling interval); occurrence-level intervals resample trajectories

keyword_vs_annotation_agentdojo.ci_note: tool-level counts are a census of the vocabulary (no sampling interval); occurrence-level intervals resample trajectories by suite|user_task cluster

keyword_vs_annotation_agentdojo_P0.ci_note: tool-level counts are a census of the vocabulary (no sampling interval); occurrence-level intervals resample trajectories by suite|user_task cluster

post_injection_proxy.definition: calls after the first step whose observation carries the injection text (located from the raw run's `injections` field); AgentDojo has no per-call hijack label, so this is a proxy

review_reported_values.source: REVIEW_REPORT.md, comment M5 (Evidence) and m8; quoted for comparison only

deviations: F1. Bootstrap for AgentDojo quantities. Plan 3.5 prescribes suite|user_task cluster resampling for the within-AgentDojo UT analyses; it is used here as the primary interval for every AgentDojo P0 quantity (WUT, and also R4 transfer and the univariate AUROCs on P0, which use the same rows), with the stratified trajectory bootstrap as a sensitivity. AgentDrift R1/R3 use the stratified trajectory bootstrap (plan 3.5), with a world-cluster sensitivity for the observation-length ablations.

F2. Tests and multiplicity. Two-sided percentile-bootstrap p-values, p = min(1, 2 min((1 + #{d <= 0})/(B + 1), (1 + #{d >= 0})/(B + 1))), so the smallest attainable value with B = 2000 is 0.001. Holm is applied across the five R3 folds separately for each contrast and metric, and, for within-minus-transfer, across the five detectors of that table only (plan family d restricted to the detectors computed here).

F3. Added detector LR-obsonly (logistic regression on max_obs and mean_obs only, cache recipe). It is not in the plan's detector list; it reproduces the review's 'observation features alone' numbers and is reported as post hoc.

F4. Coefficient intervals are not specified by the plan. R1: 500 refits on stratified resamples of data/train.jsonl (vocabulary fixed). WUT: mean, minimum and maximum over the 25 fold models, plus a descriptive model fitted on all P0 rows with 500 suite|user_task cluster-bootstrap refits.

F5. Padding specifics the plan leaves open: the filler is the sentence ' The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.' repeated and cut to exactly n characters, appended to the observation string; only positives are padded, negatives and training data are unchanged; recall uses the unchanged training threshold t_r80. In AgentDojo (WUT) the injected step(s) are located from the raw run's `injections` field; 9 of 2,294 compromised P0 traces have no located step and stay unpadded (results are also given on the located subset). Only lengthening is tested; in AgentDojo longer observations raise the attack score, so the evasive direction there would be shortening, which was not tested. The GRU is padded in R1 only (the task asked for WUT LR-C).

F6. The three R1 GRU seeds were retrained for the padding test with gru_detector.train_gru and gru_ladder.stratified_val (as the cache). Thresholds and t_r80 predictions equal the cache exactly and pool-E AUROC is identical, but 1-2 of 1,881 scores per seed differ from the cache by at most 6e-8 (float32 rounding; not bitwise identical as the GRU cache README reports for its own refit). All padding levels use the refitted models.

F7. Prevalence-weighted AUPRC (plan 3.1) is reported at pi = 0.01, 0.05 and 0.10 for the ablation tables; the plan does not fix the grid for this analysis. The t05 operating point is not reported here.

F8. The state-change annotation (tool_state_annotation.json) was made by a single annotator (an AI assistant working for the authors) from tool names, example arguments and example observations. It was not blind: the keyword list was known and the listing also showed each tool's call count and step-label counts (how often it is a hijacked step or occurs in attacked runs). 13 AgentDrift labels and 1 AgentDojo label are marked ambiguous. No second rater, so no agreement statistic.

F9. Bootstrap seeds aligned across parts (second run of this script, 2026-09-27). In the first run each part drew its own bootstrap resamples, so the same quantity (for example R4 LR-B AUROC) had slightly different intervals in the ablation, padding and annotation tables. The padding (R1 linear, R1 GRU, WUT) and annotation-sensitivity parts now use the resampling seed of the matching setting in the ablation part (9200 + setting index; 9300 + index for the sensitivity bootstrap), so identical quantities have identical intervals. Point estimates and fitted models are unchanged; only interval endpoints moved, by at most a few thousandths.
